engine / docker / layers

Golden L1–L4 Docker layers

OS base, runtime, dependencies, service code — four cached layers so rebuilds take seconds, not minutes. Golden images are shared across every service in the stack.

l1_base_layers.star — real generator
# L1 Base Layers — OS and Runtime Foundation
BUN_BASE = "oven/bun:1.3.11-alpine"
ALPINE_BASE = "alpine:3.18"

def L1_generate_os_base(base_image = None, use_golden = True):
    # Golden L1 image: deps pre-installed, CVE-patched
    if base_image == None:
        base_image = GOLDEN_L1_IMAGE if use_golden else ALPINE_BASE
engine / infisical

cli / commands

A CLI that operates the whole stack

Not just up and down — doctor diagnostics, a live terminal UI, network management, stack snapshots and safe upgrades.

terminal
$ tdk up          # boot the stack, selective startup
$ tdk ui          # live terminal dashboard
$ tdk doctor      # diagnose ports, images, secrets
$ tdk status      # health of every service
$ tdk networks    # routing topology, conflict-free
$ tdk stacks      # snapshot & switch stacks
$ tdk upgrade     # safe engine upgrades

Honest answers

The same answers we give in engineering reviews.

We need Kubernetes for production

Local dev doesn't need to match production. Use TDK for fast local iteration — 5s startup — and K8s for prod when you're ready. Fully decoupled, zero lock-in: everything TDK generates is standard Docker and TypeScript tooling.

What about CI/CD?

TDK is completely decoupled from your CI. Use it for local development and whatever you want for CI/CD. Nothing to migrate away from later.

Should we fire our DevOps team?

No. TDK removes the local-environment babysitting — setup scripts, port conflicts, rotting onboarding docs. Your infrastructure people keep production and CI/CD; product engineers stop waiting on them. Teams without a DevOps hire can simply skip making one.

Where do the savings numbers come from?

Transparent math: 5 hours per dev per week recovered, salary ÷ 2,080 working hours, plus one avoided platform-engineer role ($150K/yr) or $500/dev/month in cloud sandboxes. Try the calculator above with your own numbers.

Is 120+ services locally realistic?

Yes — with selective startup you run only what you're working on, and golden L1–L4 image layers keep rebuilds near-instant. The discovery daemon watches your repos and regenerates only what changed. Our daily driver is a 16 GB MacBook, and it performs superbly.
